description: User directed 2026-11-19: "add the elixir parity issues as tickets to the epic we gave to Elixir Parity". Owner: Elixir Parity. Found by JSON walking the json.erl port (/Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-752-walk/walk.md, fz2 from #786 head). After a FunctionClauseError, catch kind, reason binds %FunctionClauseError{} in fz; Elixir's catch normalisation binds the raw :function_clause. Done: catch sees what Elixir's sees, on three paths.

comments.text: HOLD (2026-11-24, relayed by Elixir Parity): the user is reconsidering the whole approach — raise structs natively, convert only at a catch that reads the reason. Nothing mue.28-related proceeds until decided.

User decision 2026-11-24 (in Elixir Parity's session): "let's go with the cheaper shape". fz raises exception structs natively for its own errors, as before this ticket. rescue converts only raw terms a program raised itself (:erlang.error(term)). A catch clause that binds or tests the reason translates fz's runtime-error structs back to Elixir's Erlang reasons (%FunctionClauseError{} -> :function_clause, %MatchError{term: t} -> {:badmatch, t}, ...); a catch _, _ costs nothing. Known deviation, to be tracked in its own ticket: a user-raised ArgumentError and fz's own :badarg look the same to a catch that reads the reason. This replaces the reason-raising design and the page ../fz-mue.28.html (rescue as Elixir compiles it).

title: catch kind, reason normalises a FunctionClauseError as Elixir does
